title: How Trying to Fall Asleep Backfires
description:
At the University of Virginia in 1996, volunteers who tried to fall asleep as fast as possible while brass marching music played ended up lying awake much longer than volunteers who did not try at all. Under stress, forcing sleep turns on a mental monitor that keeps checking whether you are still awake.

In 2018, sleep researchers at Baylor University wired 57 young adults to overnight brain monitors and gave them five minutes to write on paper before bed. People who listed finished tasks took 25.1 minutes to fall asleep, while people who wrote a specific to-do list for tomorrow fell asleep in 15.8 minutes as their hippocampus and prefrontal cortex stood down.

Research: Scullin et al., Baylor University (2018).
pinned_comment: Do you fall asleep faster on the living room couch than you do once you actually climb into bed?
